chunks.arabic_text: اَلْكَافِي: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَقُولُ: تَذَاكُرُ الْعِلْمِ بَيْنَ عِبَادِي مِمَّا يُحْيِي الْقُلُوبَ الْمَيِّتَةَ إِذَا هُمْ انْتَهَوْا فِيهِ إِلَى أَمْرِي

translations.en: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Discussion of knowledge between My slaves is among that which enlivens the dead hearts, if they lead them to My command.'

en.summary: This hadith highlights the spiritual efficacy of discussing religious knowledge among believers. It states that such discourse can revive spiritually dead hearts, provided that the discussion ultimately leads the participants to submit to God's command.
en.seo_question: How does discussing religious knowledge affect the heart according to Shia hadith?
